evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography, preface to Bi Xiujie, *Shangdai jinwen quanbian*
evidence.field: discussion of 元 oracle bone and Shang bronze forms
evidence.text: The article identifies the graph’s original sense as ‘human head.’ It describes two oracle-bone forms, Heji 00006 and 18747: a head rendered as a linearized square or as a long horizontal stroke with a short stroke above. It compares a Shang bronze form on the *Bei Yuan zuo fu Wu you* and says it depicts a human head. This supports the head interpretation, but does not establish that the strokes specifically represent a person 儿 plus the numeral 二.
evidence.title: 畢秀潔博士《商代金文全編》出版

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 元 entry
evidence.field: 形義通解; dated graph uses and citations
evidence.text: The entry analyzes early forms as 人 with a round point or square highlighting the head, with the mark sometimes reduced to a horizontal stroke; an extra short stroke could be added decoratively. It reports oracle-bone 元卜 in Heji 23390 as ‘first divination’; bronze uses include 元年 on the Western Zhou mid-period 師酉簋 (‘first year’), 元德 on 番生簋蓋 (‘great virtue’), and other senses ‘first,’ ‘eldest,’ and ‘special-use.’ It notes the graph is not attested with the literal ‘head’ sense in its cited oracle-bone or bronze examples, while that sense occurs in the transmitted *Zuo zhuan* and *Mengzi*. The account reports a proposal that 元 and 兀 are a split from one graph, and separately records an alternative proposal taking the two upper strokes as 上 over 人; it argues the latter is not based on the most pictorial early shape, which has a dot.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：字頭「元」

evidence.source: 國學大全, *Shuowen jiezi* and Duan Yucai annotation, 元 entry
evidence.text: The received *Shuowen* text reads 元, ‘beginning,’ 从一从兀. Duan Yucai emends/interprets the analysis as 从一，兀聲 and argues from phonological comparison that 元 and 兀 were level-tone and entering-tone counterparts in Old Chinese. Xu Kai’s *Shuowen xizhuan* instead rejects 聲 and treats the form as associative, with 兀 contributing the head sense. This is a real disagreement in how the received analysis is construed; neither medieval analysis independently proves the graph’s original formation.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text with later commentary
evidence.title: 元 说文解字

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 元 entry
evidence.text: The entry lists oracle-bone examples, multiple bronze examples, Chu manuscript, small seal, and Qin slip forms, including late Shang/early Western Zhou bronze and mid-Western Zhou 師酉簋. The cited textual labels document stages and examples, but the page’s glyph images were not visually inspected here; no claim is made about individual stroke-by-stroke changes between every stage.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 元 entry
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes graph history from lexical senses: the oracle-bone citation 元卜 is interpreted as ‘first divination’; bronze inscriptions use 元 for ‘first/beginning’ and also ‘great.’ It cites *Zuo zhuan*, Duke Xi 33, 狄人歸其元, for ‘head,’ and *Mengzi*, Teng Wen Gong II, 勇士不忘喪其元, for ‘head.’ These transmitted-text citations establish older documented usage in their respective texts, but this research did not verify composition dates or manuscript dates and does not treat them as dated physical inscriptions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：字頭「元」

evidence.field: 傳, account of the battle at Ji
evidence.text: The transmitted text states 狄人歸其元，面如生, describing the Di returning Xian Zhen’s head, its face still lifelike. This is a clear textual instance of 元 meaning ‘head’; the online text is not a manuscript dating witness.

gaps: The candidate seal-script SVGs were not opened or visually inspected; therefore no image-based glyph observation, provenance decision, or asset-rights recommendation is made.

The claim that the graph depicts a human head is supported by specialist and university paleographic accounts, but exact identification of the figure strokes as 儿 plus 二 is not established and is not repeated as a historical fact.

The proposed 人+上 analysis is reported as a scholarly alternative by the CUHK entry and disputed there on the basis of the dot-form variant; no primary publication presenting its full argument was independently inspected.

The received *Shuowen* wording varies in interpretation: its transmitted line says 从一从兀; Xu Kai rejects a phonetic marker, while Duan Yucai reads 兀 as phonetic. No manuscript collation was consulted to resolve textual history.

Early head sense and later/attested first-beginning uses are separable: the cited oracle-bone and bronze examples support beginning/first, while the graph’s proposed head referent is not found in those cited inscriptional examples. The semantic transition from head to first/beginning is plausible and stated by the paleographic dictionary, but the exact historical path is not documented by a sequence of dated examples here.

No exact date for the Heji 23390 oracle-bone inscription or the cited bronze inscriptions was established in the opened pages; period labels only are reported. Composition dates of the transmitted *Zuo zhuan* and *Mengzi* examples were not independently researched.

The dataset’s Baxter–Sagart row was supplied locally and preserves its exact notation, but no external upstream table was accessed. The official Unicode character lookup page was attempted twice and returned an internal error; Unicode’s general documentation cannot substitute for verifying the character-specific kMandarin record.

No sound component is proposed for 元 in the graphic account, so no component-versus-host historical pronunciation comparison is applicable. The Shang pronunciation/source word underlying the graph is not independently reconstructed by the consulted sources.

The inspected CUHK page identifies relevant graph stages and individual inscription examples, but the page’s glyph images were not visually inspected here; the proposed image is a seal-script redraw and cannot illustrate artifact-specific stroke details.
Exact inscription dates for Heji 23390 and the cited bronze examples were not established beyond their inscriptional period/context labels.
Xiaoxuetang was considered but no exact 元 record page and selected image URL were verified, so no Xiaoxuetang asset is proposed.
The exact ACC-s00003.svg Commons page could not be opened in this run; it is not proposed despite search-result metadata. No claim is made from its inaccessible page beyond the search result summary.
